newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary ratifies friendship treaty with Romania.
newsitem.headline: Hungary ratifies friendship treaty with Romania.

text.p: Hungary's parliament has ratified a friendship treaty with Romania in a move that could help the two former Warsaw Pact members join the European Union and NATO.

A majority of members in Hungary's National Assembly ratified the treaty in a vote late on Tuesday, in a bid to end decades of tension between the neighbours over the status of Romania's 1.6 million ethnic Hungarians.

Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs told members of Hungary's one-tier legislature that while the treaty was a big step forward, no one expected it to iron out every difference between the two countries overnight.
"The document is regarded (here and), also abroad, as a step towards reconciliation to be reached in a European manner," Kovacs said.
Hungarian newpapers reported on Wednesday that 249 voted in favour, 53 were against and there were 12 abstentions.
Romania's Senate ratified the treaty in September and its lower Chamber of Deputies approved the treaty in October.
Hungarian opposition politicians criticised the ruling coalition of Socialists and Free Democrats, who swung the vote with their majority, saying they had acted too hastily.
Gyorgy Csoti of the opposition party MDF was quoted by the national MTI news agency as saying that his party had voted against the treaty because it was weak and incomplete.
Hungary's right-wing opposition have criticised the treaty, saying it still failed to guarantee sufficient rights for Romania's ethnic Hungarians.
